EduBrisk at Chinmaya Vidyalaya, Virugambakkam this year

What you are looking at

This page is built from two records kept by the platform: every test a student attempted, with the mark and date of each try, and the time each student spent signed in. Nothing here is estimated — each figure counts actual rows in those records.

The charts below read across all grades at once. Pick a grade from the filter above and they step aside for that grade’s own subject, chapter and test tables.

Click any student in the engagement chart to open their record — hours, attempts, average mark and every subject mark. Hovering any point or row shows its exact figures.

Summary

Where this comes from
The platform's test-attempt export for Grades 6–10, matched against the class list the school supplied. The export carries one row per attempt, so a student who sat the same test twice is two rows there but one student here.
What it shows
How many of the students on roll in the current selection have attempted at least one test, and how those attempts divide between a first try and later ones.
What it does not show
Whether a test was set as classwork or homework or taken voluntarily, and whether a student who did not attempt was absent or simply never opened the platform.
Who is not in it
Anyone not on the class list the school supplied. An attempt under a name the class list does not carry was set aside rather than guessed at.

These attempts come from another grade's file and are not counted in this grade's figures.

Evidence of impact

Across every grade. Click a grade on the left-hand chart to open it.

Where this comes from
The same attempt export. Only students who attempted the same test more than once feed the left-hand chart; the right-hand one counts every student at the end of each month.
What it shows
Where a second attempt took students — their mark on the first try against the best mark of their later tries — and how the number of students reached grew through the year.
What it does not show
Cause. A student who chooses to retake a test is usually one who means to do better, so this is the gain on retakes, not proof that the platform alone produced it.
Who is not in it
Students who attempted every test only once. They are in the reach chart but nowhere in the first-to-second-attempt chart.

Engagement against attainment

Where this comes from
Across the bottom: the number of tests the student has attempted, from the platform export. Up the side: the student's average internal mark — the school's own assessment marks as held in iAspire, not EduBrisk marks.
What it shows
Whether the students putting in practice on the platform are also the students scoring well in school assessments.
What it does not show
Cause, in either direction. The dashed lines are the medians of this selection only, so a label such as “Strong and engaged” means above the middle of this group on both counts — not a verdict against any outside standard. Change the grade or section and the lines move with it.
Who is not in it
Students with no internal mark on record; the number left out is printed under the chart. Students with no attempts are kept, in the lane on the left.

Class view

Where this comes from
One bubble per student in the selected section. Position is tests attempted against average internal mark from iAspire; colour is the student's average mark on EduBrisk tests; size is time spent on the platform.
What it shows
Four things about one class at once — who is practising, who is scoring in school, who is scoring on the platform, and who is spending time without it showing in either.
What it does not show
Size is scaled by rank within the class, not in proportion: a bubble twice the size is not twice the hours, only further up the class. Colour is banded in fifteen-point steps.
Who is not in it
Students with no internal mark. Students with no EduBrisk mark yet are shown in the palest colour and counted under the chart.

Subject-wise participation

Click a subject to see its tests.

Where this comes from
The attempt export, grouped by the subject each test belongs to.
What it shows
For each subject, how many students on roll have attempted at least one of its tests and how many have attempted none.
What it does not show
How well students did, and whether the chapters attempted match what the class has actually been taught so far.
Who is not in it
Subjects a grade has not been given on the platform — they do not appear at all.

Logins and coverage

Where this comes from
The platform's usage export, matched to the class list by name.
What it shows
How many accounts have been signed into at least once, and how many never have.
What it does not show
How often or how recently a student signs in. One sign-in in the whole year counts the same as daily use.
Who is not in it
Students the usage export does not carry — they are counted separately rather than assumed to have never signed in.

Section-wise participation

Where this comes from
The same export, grouped by the section each student sits in on the class list.
What it shows
Participation section by section for whatever subject or chapter is selected above.
What it does not show
It does not separate a section that was never set the work from one that was set it and did not do it.
Who is not in it
Students whose section is blank on the class list.

Achiever-level participation

Where this comes from
Achiever levels come from the school's internal assessment marks in iAspire. They are not derived from anything on EduBrisk.
What it shows
Whether participation differs between higher, middle and lower achievers.
What it does not show
Current standing. The level is fixed from the assessment it was taken from and does not move with platform results.
Who is not in it
Students with no internal mark on record carry no level, so they sit outside this table — they are still counted everywhere else.

Cross-test glance

Where this comes from
Every attempt on the tests in the selected chapter. A filled cell holds the best mark of that student's attempts.
What it shows
One row per student across all the tests in a chapter, so the gaps show up in a single view.
What it does not show
How many attempts produced the mark shown, or when it was taken.
Who is not in it
No one. Every student on roll in the selection has a row, whether they have taken anything or not.

Test-wise participation

Where this comes from
The attempt export, grouped by individual test.
What it shows
How many students attempted each test in the current selection, and how many did not.
What it does not show
Whether the test was assigned, and how long students were given.
Who is not in it
Tests nobody has attempted. The export is built from attempts, so a test with none does not appear.
